橡皮筋来回动，带动附近的空气振动，声音就能传到耳朵。轻轻按住橡皮筋，振动很快停止: The band moves back and forth and makes nearby air vibrate, allowing sound to reach your ears. Gently holding the band quickly stops its vibration and its sound.
同样长、同样粗的橡皮筋，绷得更紧时通常振得更快，音调更高。在这幅简化图里，拨得更: For a band of the same length and thickness, more tension usually makes it vibrate faster with a higher pitch. In this simplified model, a bigger pluck mainly makes the sound louder, not higher.
先只改变绷紧程度，听音调高低。再保持绷紧程度不变，只改变拨动幅度：主要改变的是声: First change only the tension and listen to pitch. Then keep tension fixed and change how far you pluck: does loudness or pitch change most?
采用固定两端的理想弦基频关系 f = (1/2L)√(T/μ)。保持长度 L 和: The fundamental frequency of an ideal string fixed at both ends is f = (1/2L)√(T/μ). With length L and linear density μ fixed, quadrupling tension T doubles frequency. Stretching a real rubber band also changes length and linear density and introduces nonlinear effects and damping. Sound here is synthesized to demonstrate frequency and amplitude, not recorded from a rubber band.
画面使用约百倍慢镜头和放大的位移；弧线仅提示声音向外传播，空气不随声音一路飞到耳: Motion is slowed by roughly one hundred times and displacement is enlarged. Arcs only suggest outward sound propagation; air does not travel all the way to the ear with the sound. Manual slow motion changes display phase without playing audio. Playback requires a click and stops when the page is hidden or left. An adult should inspect real rubber bands; never stretch or snap them toward a face.
两端拉开和橡皮筋变细是绷紧动作的视觉提示，不用于计算实际伸长量；音高仍采用上述固: The outward pull and thinner band are visual cues for tightening, not a calculation of extension. Pitch still follows the fixed-length teaching model above.
先播放，再切换到空气。金色小团的“家”用空心圈标出。: Start the motion, then switch to air. The open circle marks the gold parcel’s home position.
橡皮筋附近先开始动；远处要等一等，变化才传得到。: Air near the band responds first. Farther away, the disturbance takes time to arrive.
金色空气小团只在空心圈附近来回；疏密变化继续向右传。: The gold parcel moves back and forth near its open circle while compressions and rarefactions travel right.
声源已经停下，先前发出的变化仍在空气中继续前进。: The source has stopped, but the disturbance already emitted is still traveling through the air.
最后一段变化已经离开。空气小团回到各自的平衡位置。: The final disturbance has passed. Air parcels return to their equilibrium positions.
播放一次实际音高；慢镜头可以独立暂停。: Playing the actual pitch once; slow motion can be paused separately.
声音暂时无法播放，仍可观察慢镜头。: Audio is unavailable, but you can still inspect the slow motion.
金色实心点：同一小团空气: Gold dot: the same air parcel
慢镜头不自动发声。听声音需要单独点击。: Slow motion is silent. Click the audio button to hear the pitch.
橡皮筋来回动，带动附近的空气振动，声音就能传到耳朵。声源停下来以后，已经发出的声: The band moves back and forth, disturbing nearby air so sound can reach an ear. After the source stops, waves already emitted keep traveling and end a little later farther away.
模型保持弦长和线密度不变，张力只影响频率。空气视图是同一声源的局部平面纵波示意；: The model fixes string length and linear density; tension changes frequency. The air view illustrates a local plane longitudinal wave driven by the same source. Dots show the mean positions of air parcels, not the thermal motion of individual molecules.
画面把时间和位移大幅放慢、放大，用延迟的同一振动表示传播；图中距离和秒数不能换算: Time is greatly slowed and displacement enlarged. Delayed copies of the same vibration show propagation; diagram distances and seconds do not measure real sound speed. Shading indicates relative compression, omitting 3D spreading, reflections and thermal motion. Changing conditions resets the experiment; scrubbing is silent. Hiding or leaving the page stops playback. Ask an adult to check real rubber bands and keep stretched bands away from faces.

追踪声源、空气、鼓膜与耳蜗，比较音高、幅度和传播条件，区分机械振动与神经消息。: Trace the source, air, eardrum and cochlea; compare pitch, amplitude and transmission, and distinguish mechanical vibration from neural signals.
拨动一根弦，为什么远处的耳朵会收到消息？先跟着振动旅行，再改变一个条件，看看什么: Why can a distant ear receive a message when a string is plucked? Follow the vibration, then change one condition to discover what changes and what stays the same.
振动 → 介质传递 → 耳内机械响应 → 电信号: Vibration → transmission through a medium → ear mechanics → electrical signals
沿途传递的是扰动与能量，不是一小团空气从弦一路跑进脑里。切换窗口会暂停动画，保留: Disturbances and energy pass along the route; a parcel of air does not run from the string into the brain. Switching windows pauses motion and preserves each study’s progress.
两个慢镜头共用音高与幅度的比较条件，但不是同一条真实时间尺。耳蜗位置只示意高低音: The two slow-motion studies share pitch and amplitude comparisons, not a real-time clock. Cochlear position illustrates the direction of a pitch difference, not anatomical locations for 196–392 Hz, decibels or hearing ability.
只改变一个条件，才能看清原因: Change one condition to see its effect
上面的三个条件会同时改变这里的曲线和前两站的实验。浅灰色是起始条件，彩色是当前条: The three presets change these curves and the previous studies together. Light gray marks the starting condition and color the current one. Every horizontal axis spans 20 milliseconds; vertical axes share an illustrative amplitude scale.
声源：往返次数还是摆动大小？: Source: more cycles or larger motion?
相同时间窗口内，比较声源振动的频率和幅度: Compare frequency and amplitude within the same time window
传播：中间还需要什么？: Transmission: what must be in between?
真空，没有其他接触路径: Vacuum, with no other contact path
比较有空气和真空时，路径中的声压变化: Compare pressure variation in air with a vacuum path
曲线画的是某一位置随时间的变化，不是空气在空间里走出的波浪路线。右图为稳态局部对: The curves show change over time at one location, not wavy paths traveled by air. The right plot compares steady local behavior, not arrival times; see the first study for propagation delay. Vacuum applies only to this separate experiment, not to the earlier ear animation.
同样的音高，为什么可以轻一些或响一些？: Why can the same pitch sound softer or louder?
频率描述每秒振动多少次；振幅描述偏离平衡位置多远。保持频率，只改变振幅，曲线会长: Frequency counts cycles per second; amplitude measures departure from equilibrium. Changing amplitude at fixed frequency makes a curve taller without adding cycles. Perceived loudness also depends on frequency, duration and individual differences, so this is not a sound-level meter.
可以，桌子和绳子也能传递机械振动。真空对照假设声源与接收端之间既没有空气，也没有: Yes: tables and strings can carry mechanical vibrations. Our vacuum comparison assumes neither air nor a solid bridge connects source and receiver. A real support can transmit sound; that is not sound traveling through a vacuum.
听见，并不只是鼓膜动了一下: Hearing involves more than a moving eardrum
耳蜗里的机械变化会影响感觉细胞，再影响神经放电。脑需要继续处理这些消息，我们才能: Mechanical changes in the cochlea affect sensory cells, which influence nerve firing. Further processing in the brain lets us recognize sounds. The purple line is not an air-filled tube.
继续追问：真实声音为什么更复杂？: Ask further: why are real sounds more complex?
单一频率的曲线方便比较，但真实橡皮筋、乐器和说话声通常包含多个频率，还会随时间起: Single-frequency curves simplify comparison, but real bands, instruments and voices usually contain multiple changing frequencies. Timbre differs from pitch, and a frequency does not activate just one cochlear point. Full spectra, outer-hair-cell feedback and recognition in the brain are not modeled here.
这是条件对照，不是声压、声速或听力测量。合成试听仅在第一站主动点击时短暂播放，请: This is a conditions comparison, not a measurement of pressure, sound speed or hearing. A brief synthesized tone plays only when explicitly requested in the first study. Keep device volume comfortable; headphones and high volume are unnecessary.
20 毫秒内约 {{cycles}} 次往返。比较灰色参考线：是周期数量变了，还: About {{cycles}} cycles in 20 milliseconds. Compare with the gray reference: has the number of cycles changed, or the curve’s height?
空气提供传递扰动的介质。这里保留频率，不模拟传播损耗；不是小团空气从声源跑到耳朵: Air provides a medium for the disturbance. Frequency is preserved here; transmission losses are not modeled. Air parcels do not run from the source to the ear.
声源仍能振动，但理想真空路径没有介质传声。没有空气，也没有连接两端的固体。: The source can still vibrate, but the ideal vacuum path has no medium to carry sound: neither air nor a solid connects the ends.
这里接收同一组音高与幅度条件；位置变化只表示趋势，不把合成音的赫兹数换算成耳蜗坐: This study receives the same pitch and amplitude comparison. Position indicates a trend, not a conversion from synthesized hertz to anatomical cochlear coordinates.
这一站沿用声源的音高与幅度条件（当前合成音约 {{hz}} Hz），并从鼓膜附近: This stop keeps the source's pitch and amplitude settings (synthesized tone about {{hz}} Hz) and magnifies the region near the eardrum. The two slow-motion views do not share a real-time clock; cochlear position shows a qualitative trend.
同一段扰动已经走到右端。这里放大看鼓膜怎样接住它。: The same disturbance has reached the receiver at the right. Here we enlarge how the eardrum responds.
这里从声波到达鼓膜时放大观察；想看它怎样传来，可以回到第一站。: This close-up begins when the sound reaches the eardrum. Return to the first stop to see how it travels here.

空气镜头用 u(x,t)=uₛ(t−x/vₑ) 把同一次有限声源振动延迟到不同位: The air view uses u(x,t)=uₛ(t−x/vₑ) to delay the same finite source vibration at each position; vₑ=145 diagram units per teaching second. The receiver is 688 diagram units from the source, so the front arrives around teaching second 4.74 and the trailing edge passes around 13.74 after the source has stopped. Diagram time and distance cannot be converted into a real sound speed. Reflections, attenuation and absolute sound pressure are not calculated.
